requirements.requirement: Run a long-running background worker on node1 as a managed service named inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: OpenRC shows inventory-worker enabled in the default runlevel and running. Its heartbeat advanced over time before the reboot and again after automatic post-reboot recovery.

requirements.requirement: Confine the worker so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory.
requirements.summary: The live worker's process root is /var/lib/inventory, it runs as the unprivileged inventory account, and its observed heartbeat output is stored beneath that tree. The same confinement was directly observed after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the worker gains no new privileges.
requirements.summary: Live process status before and after reboot shows NoNewPrivs=1, UID/GID set to inventory, and zero effective and ambient capabilities.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct runtime evidence. inventory-worker is managed by OpenRC, remains active and productive, is chroot-confined to /var/lib/inventory, and runs without new privileges. The mandatory node restart was also fully evidenced and showed successful persistent recovery.
limitations: No explicit attempted write to a host path outside /var/lib/inventory was captured; confinement is instead established by the live process root, unprivileged identity, and observed output location.
The generic lifecycle failed-services probe is systemd-specific and unsupported on Alpine, but direct OpenRC status checks cover the task service.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Service and sandbox creation were required implementation work; failed initial service configurations were promptly corrected. The bounded chroot-test and direct-test diagnostic files contributed to troubleshooting and were removed by cmd-0e4409fe656d42b1. Lifecycle comparison shows no new temporary-file residue, package inconsistency, or listening service exposure. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart service and data, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot ID corroborated by fixed lifecycle observations, and recovered service, confinement, privilege state, and advancing data.
